body:
Does it happen with 0bbaef8 ? (which is before https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/10059 was merged). cc @jerdna-regeiz

PVS analyzer found ~10 new issues: https://github.com/neovim/doc/commit/ba7a856003ccc75bbb0d8054fdc298d7295986cf

I took some holidays on may 23rd, was back home yesterday and then updated my neovim installation. never had any crash before. since commit 0bbaef8 is 2 days old I think I can say that it did not happen before merge, but if you need to be 100% sure I'll try to see how can I tell homebrew to compile a specific commit

@zchee thanks, I also noticed that in the PR https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/10059#issuecomment-496019423 . If reverting 51563b7 fixes the segfault then this is most likely an intentional constraint.

@justinmk No, I tried to revert only 51563b7(~~plus adding this, needs compile, https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/83025f0028ee5b1b6e09340fa419999643e3f8f6#diff-380a3338a107482ea09b61a4b8c98a8cR323~~), but segfault again. 

**EDIT**: 
> _plus adding this, needs compile_

which is my git revert misoperation. ignore it. actually, deleted on 8df9213d1b6ed804fb883073e012b82d26080963

> PVS analyzer found ~10 new issues: [neovim/doc@ba7a856](https://github.com/neovim/doc/commit/ba7a856003ccc75bbb0d8054fdc298d7295986cf)

Had a look at those, but as far as I can see those new ones are all the result of checks against null pointers from allocs (oom), which may not occur in neovim. I should probably go through them and remove the unnecessary checks, but I guess the cause for the segfault is not on that list. 

The `insert_sign_by_lnum_prio` does only walk the signlist backwards until a sign with higher priority is found. For how this can segfault my guess is a path where a sign (or rather the signlist entry) is freed but not removed from the signlist.

Does anyone have a reliable way to trigger that segfault? Does it only occur on mac?

Gave up for today, but had a last thought (which I could not verify, because I lack the neovim knowledge).

May it occur that insert_sign and/or buf_delsign are called parallel from different threads? Both functions are not thread safe in the way they alter the linked list. (could explain the randomness)

@jerdna-regeiz I don't have a 100% reliable way, but [coc.nvim](https://github.com/neoclide/coc.nvim) + [coc-git](https://github.com/neoclide/coc-git) with `git.enableGutters` set to `true` seems to trigger it somewhat reliably after entering insert mode and changing a line.

Once `git.enableGutters` is set to `false`, I'm unable to reproduce the issue.

@nifoc I confirm the behaviour. But even after disabling `coc-git` it randomly exits with SIGSEGV.
I have a similar setup of the author of the issue: `nvim 0.4.0-dev` + `coc.nvim` + `fish-shell`
I can also reproduce it with `nvim 0.4.0-dev` + `coc.nvim`, but I'm on `zsh` rather than `fish`.

I quess I found something.
Can anyone please test the commit https://github.com/jerdna-regeiz/neovim/commit/0b11664c6b4b5b0c782986c8edb1fa9c86e32af6 in branch https://github.com/jerdna-regeiz/neovim/tree/segfault_with_signs_10078? At least for me it prevents the found endless loop. I got my hopes up that it fixes both issues.
For now it breaks a neovim testcase (sorting of signs), but if the commit fixes the segfault I'll restore the correct behaviour in other ways.
